review_method: Visual inspection of 16 Illumina PNG schematics, cached catalogue text, and targeted primary-paper passages. No new native model extraction run and no independent reviewer.

diagram_anchors: Separate the DNA and the RNA
cases.shared: Cell isolation/lysis, oligo(dT)-based physical separation of RNA and DNA, and a Smart-seq2-based transcriptome branch.
cases.change: The DNA-processing branch uses single-cell bisulfite sequencing for methylome profiling rather than the MDA genome-amplification branch shown in the G&T schematic.
cases.why_it_matters: Physical separation enables DNA bisulfite processing without subjecting the transcriptome to that conversion, while retaining same-cell pairing.
cases.history: The scM&T primary paper explicitly describes application of scBS-seq to DNA purified by the G&T-seq protocol. This is positive development evidence.
qualifications: MDA is the implementation shown by Illumina, not an immutable definition of every G&T-seq variant.
The poster label compresses scBS-seq into an amplification branch; its methylation-conversion and library logic should not be interpreted as ordinary MDA.
cases.source_locator: Main text paragraph beginning We and others have recently described; Online Methods, Sample collection & Single-cell sequencing.
cases.short_quote: allowing bisulfite conversion of DNA without affecting the transcriptome
cases.representation_conclusion: Match the shared connected prefix and RNA branch; locate the change on the DNA branch. Do not describe two whole assays as either entirely identical or entirely different.

cases.shared: Droplet compartmentalization and cell-associated barcoded oligonucleotides supporting pooled single-cell RNA measurements.
cases.change: Drop-seq captures RNA on bead-bound primers, recovers the beads and performs reverse transcription in bulk. Original inDrop photo-releases primers and performs barcoding reverse transcription inside intact droplets before breakup.
cases.why_it_matters: The physical carrier and the point at which a cell-associated transcript becomes covalently encoded differ. A collection of intact droplets is not a common mixed solution of their contents.
cases.history: The inspected evidence establishes shared purpose and mechanistic differences, not a directed development edge between these two methods.
qualifications: Pooling intact droplets does not imply droplet breakup.
Do not infer bulk reverse transcription merely from the position of a broad cDNA synthesis caption after collection.
Restrict this comparison to the cited original implementations.
source_locators: Drop-seq: Sequencing and analysis of many STAMPs in a single reaction.
inDrop: Figure 1 and A microfluidic platform for droplet barcoding and analysis of single cells.
short_quotes: we break droplets, collect the mRNA-bound microparticles
primers are photo-released by ultraviolet exposure
cases.representation_conclusion: Record what is pooled, whether compartments persist, where primers are attached/released, and when reverse transcription occurs. A generic pooling label cannot define an interchangeable component.

diagram_anchors: Add semi-random primers and AzNTPs - dNTP mixture
cases.shared: RNA abundance is interrogated through a DNA sequencing library, with joining reactions participating in library generation.
cases.change: RASL-seq uses RNA to template joining of synthetic DNA probe pairs; the sequenced products are probe-derived amplicons. ClickSeq makes RNA-derived cDNA and joins an adapter to its chemically modified end.
cases.why_it_matters: The biological analyte, reaction substrate, and sequenced proxy are different roles. Neither a ligation label nor an RNA-sequencing category identifies which molecules are joined.
cases.history: This comparison does not establish a directed historical relationship.
qualifications: Do not force reverse transcription into every RNA-measurement architecture.
The original RASL assay and its Rnl2-based refinement must be scoped separately.
ClickSeq polymerase compatibility is supported for the reported products and workflow, not every possible click-linked oligonucleotide.
source_locators: RASL: Basic Protocol, RASL reaction; sequencing and analysis.
ClickSeq: library construction and click-ligation schematic.
cases.short_quote: the aligned pairs of probes correctly annealed to their complementary templates are ligated
cases.representation_conclusion: Track molecular roles and local reactive features. Shared purpose can be retrieved without asserting a shared joining mechanism.

cases.shared: Phosphatase-containing RNA-end processing followed by adapter ligation and sequencing-library generation.
cases.change: cP-RNA-seq exploits 3-prime end chemistry and periodate resistance followed by end repair; CIP-TAP depicts selection/processing involving capped 5-prime ends, with adapter attachment at defined points in the sequence.
cases.why_it_matters: A shared reagent does not identify the same complete selection mechanism. Terminal chemistry and order determine the populations that can contribute to the library.
cases.history: No directed development edge established by the inspected diagrams.
qualifications: The cP-RNA-seq paper explicitly warns that terminal 2-prime-O-methylated RNAs can resist periodate and be sequenced without having cyclic phosphate.
CIP-TAP observations here are diagram-level; this case does not claim a complete primary-protocol verification of CIP-TAP.
cases.short_quote: these modified RNAs would not be cleaved via a periodate treatment
cases.representation_conclusion: Keep end-group states and selection limitations explicit. Do not turn enrichment into a claim of perfect molecular specificity.

cases.shared: Restriction-site-based reduced-representation DNA sequencing with adapter/barcode ligation and amplification.
cases.change: The original ddRAD paper replaces random shearing/end repair with a simultaneous two-enzyme digest and precise size selection; it also specifies a combinatorial indexing strategy.
cases.source_discrepancy: The Illumina ddRAD schematic visually places second restriction digest after barcoded-adapter addition. Its literal order does not match the cited Peterson protocol's simultaneous double digest before ligation. The grouped RAD schematic additionally suggests substituting a second digest into the shearing position.
cases.resolution: For a scientific graph of the Peterson implementation, use the primary protocol's ordering and keep a source-specific note explaining why the Illumina diagram is not followed literally. This is not an unresolved chemical impossibility.
cases.history: The primary paper explicitly states that the protocol builds on RAD-seq and describes its changes.
qualifications: This is a comparison to named original implementations, not a claim that all later RAD protocols have one invariant order.
Target size selection is part of the defining selection architecture even where absent from the compact schematic.
cases.source_locator: Results and Discussion, description beginning We have developed a protocol; Figure 2; Supporting Protocol S1.
cases.short_quote: a restriction digest with two enzymes simultaneously
cases.representation_conclusion: Diagram fidelity and primary-protocol accuracy must be assessed separately. A convenient figure is not automatically an accurate execution-order specification.

cases.shared: Antibody-mediated chromatin enrichment to associate genomic sequence with a protein or histone modification.
cases.change: ChIPmentation introduces sequencing-compatible adapters through Tn5 tagmentation directly on immunoprecipitated, bead-bound chromatin.
cases.why_it_matters: The substrate context and placement of adapter insertion are central; matching only the name tagmentation omits what it acts on and when.
cases.history: The primary ChIPmentation paper explicitly combines ChIP with Tn5-based library preparation and discusses ATAC-seq as related background.
qualifications: The grouped ChIP schematic includes exonuclease digestion. It cannot define a universal baseline for every ChIP-seq implementation.
The card's 1988 reference supports foundational ChIP work, not invention of sequencing-based ChIP-seq in 1988.
The present comparison uses the baseline described in the ChIPmentation paper, not an indiscriminate copy of the grouped Illumina row.
cases.source_locator: ChIPmentation abstract and main-text rationale for tagmenting bead-bound chromatin; publication identities for ChIP and sequencing-based ChIP.
cases.representation_conclusion: Represent reuse plus an evidenced change in substrate/interface/workflow position. Resolve method scope before computing graph differences or chronological relationships.
